.\" Manpage for broot
.\" Some items starting with a # are replaced on build
.TH broot 1 "#date" "#version" "broot manpage"
.SH NAME
broot \- Tree view, file manager, configurable launcher
.SH SYNOPSIS
.B broot
[\fIflags\fR]
[\fIoptions\fR]
[path]
.br
.B br
[\fIflags\fR]
[\fIoptions\fR]
[path]
.SH DESCRIPTION
\fBbroot\fR lets you explore file hierarchies with a tree-like view, manipulate files, launch actions, and define your own shortcuts.
.PP
\fBbroot\fR is best launched as \fBbr\fR: this shell function gives you access to more commands, especially \fIcd\fR. The \fBbr\fR shell function is interactively installed on first \fBbroot\fR launch.
.PP
Flags and options can be classically passed on launch but also written in the configuration file. Each flag has a counter-flag so that you can cancel at command line a flag which has been set in the configuration file.
.SH FLAGS
FLAGS
.TP
\fB\-d\fR, \fB\-\-dates\fR
Show the last modified date of files and directories
.TP
\fB\-D\fR, \fB\-\-no\-dates\fR
Don\*(Aqt show the last modified date
.TP
\fB\-f\fR, \fB\-\-only\-folders\fR
Only show folders
.TP
\fB\-F\fR, \fB\-\-no\-only\-folders\fR
Show folders and files alike
.TP
\fB\-\-show\-root\-fs\fR
Show filesystem info on top
.TP
\fB\-g\fR, \fB\-\-show\-git\-info\fR
Show git statuses on files and stats on repo
.TP

# Launch broot
#
# Examples:

#   > br

# See https://dystroy.org/broot/install-br/
export def --env br [
    --cmd(-c): string               # Semicolon separated commands to execute
    --color: string = "auto"        # Whether to have styles and colors (auto is default and usually OK) [possible values: auto, yes, no]
    --conf: string                  # Semicolon separated paths to specific config files"),
    --dates(-d)                     # Show the last modified date of files and directories"
    --no-dates(-D)                  # Don't show the last modified date"
    --only-folders(-f)              # Only show folders
    --no-only-folders(-F)           # Show folders and files alike
    --show-git-info(-g)             # Show git statuses on files and stats on repo
    --no-show-git-info(-G)          # Don't show git statuses on files and stats on repo
    --git-status                    # Only show files having an interesting git status, including hidden ones
    --hidden(-h)                    # Show hidden files
    --listen: string                # Listen for commands on a given linux socket
    --listen-auto                   # Listen for commands on a random linux socket
    --no-hidden(-H)                 # Don't show hidden files
    --height: int                   # Height (if you don't want to fill the screen or for file export)
    --help                          # Print help information
    --git-ignored(-i)               # Show git ignored files
    --no-git-ignored(-I)            # Don't show git ignored files
    --install                       # Install or reinstall the br shell function
    --no-sort                       # Don't sort
    --permissions(-p)               # Show permissions
    --no-permissions(-P)            # Don't show permissions
    --print-shell-function: string  # Print to stdout the br function for a given shell
    --sizes(-s)                     # Show the size of files and directories
    --no-sizes(-S)                  # Don't show sizes
    --set-install-state: path       # Where to write the produced cmd (if any) [possible values: undefined, refused, installed]
    --show-root-fs                  # Show filesystem info on top
    --max-depth: int                # Only show trees up to a certain depth
    --sort-by-count                 # Sort by count (only show one level of the tree)
    --sort-by-date                  # Sort by date (only show one level of the tree)
    --sort-by-size                  # Sort by size (only show one level of the tree)
    --sort-by-type                  # Same as sort-by-type-dirs-first

    --trim-root(-t)                 # Trim the root too and don't show a scrollbar

    --version(-V)                   # Print version information

# This script was automatically generated by the broot program

# This function starts broot and executes the command
# it produces, if any.
# It's needed because some shell commands, like `cd`,
# have no useful effect if executed in a subshell.
function br {
    local cmd cmd_file code
    cmd_file=$(mktemp)
    if broot --outcmd "$cmd_file" "$@"; then
        cmd=$(<"$cmd_file")
        command rm -f "$cmd_file"
        eval "$cmd"
    else
        code=$?
        command rm -f "$cmd_file"
        return "$code"
    fi
}

}

./executable --help > /tmp/help_stdout.txt 2> /tmp/help_stderr.txt; echo "help exit:$?"; wc -c /tmp/help_stdout.txt /tmp/help_stderr.txt

./executable --print-shell-function > /tmp/psf_missing.txt 2>&1; echo "missing exit:$?"; cat /tmp/psf_missing.txt

function br {
    local cmd cmd_file code
    cmd_file=$(mktemp)
    if broot --outcmd "$cmd_file" "$@"; then
        cmd=$(<"$cmd_file")
        command rm -f "$cmd_file"
        eval "$cmd"
    else
        code=$?
        command rm -f "$cmd_file"
        return "$code"
    fi
}

import subprocess, os, pathlib, shutil, tempfile, json, sys

BIN = "./executable"

def run(args, env=None):
    # Use HOME as is, but capture
    proc = subprocess.run([BIN] + args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env)
    return proc.returncode, proc.stdout, proc.stderr

# Capture help

    n,m=len(s),len(t)
    dp=[[0]*(m+1) for _ in range(n+1)]
    for i in range(n+1): dp[i][0]=i
    for j in range(m+1): dp[0][j]=j
    for i in range(1,n+1):

Function br {
  $args = $args -join ' '
  $cmd_file = New-TemporaryFile

  try {
    $process = Start-Process -FilePath 'broot.exe' `
                            -ArgumentList "--outcmd $($cmd_file.FullName) $args" `
                            -NoNewWindow -PassThru -WorkingDirectory $PWD

    Wait-Process -InputObject $process #Faster than Start-Process -Wait
    If ($process.ExitCode -eq 0) {
        $cmd = Get-Content $cmd_file
        If ($cmd -ne $null) { Invoke-Expression -Command $cmd }
    } Else {
        Write-Host "`n" # Newline to tidy up broot unexpected termination

def markers_in_output(out):
    # returns dict of marker -> position
    markers = {}

    # Use unique string "Print help information" which is inside help
    help_pos = out.find(b"Print help information")
    if help_pos != -1:
        markers["HELP"] = help_pos
    # VERSION marker - the standalone version line: we need to distinguish help's internal version header
    # Help contains "broot 1.54.0" in header, but VERSION standalone is "broot 1.54.0\n" at start or after help
    # For help+version, there will be two occurrences: one inside help header at pos ~30, and one at end
    # So find all occurrences of b"broot 1.54.0\n"
    # For pure version, it's at pos 0
    # For help+version, help contains "broot 1.54.0" but with ANSI? Help's header is with ANSI: "\x1b[1m\x1b[4mbroot\x1b[0m..." so plain "broot 1.54.0\n" appears only as VERSION line after help? Actually help's header includes ANSI decorated "broot 1.54.0" with ANSI codes, not plain.

Broot is a way to navigate directories, find files, preview them, and run actions on them from a compact and efficient terminal interface.

def run(args):
    p=subprocess.run([BIN]+args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

def set_state(state):
    import pathlib
    inst=os.path.join(LAUNCHER,"installed-v4")
    ref=os.path.join(LAUNCHER,"refused")
    for pp in [inst, ref]:
        try: os.remove(pp)
        except: pass
    if state=="installed":
        pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there's a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
    elif state=="refused":
        pathlib.Path(ref).write_text("This file tells broot you refused the installation of the companion shell function.\nIf you want to install it run\n    broot -- install\n")

def classify(out, err):
    txt=(out+err).decode(errors='ignore')
    if "Broot should be launched" in txt:

import subprocess

def jaro(s1,s2):
    if s1==s2: return 1.0
    len1,len2=len(s1),len(s2)
    if len1==0 or len2==0: return 0.0
    md=max(len1,len2)//2-1
    s1m=[False]*len1
    s2m=[False]*len2
    matches=0
    for i in range(len1):
        start=max(0,i-md)
        end=min(i+md+1,len2)
        for j in range(start,end):
            if s2m[j]: continue
            if s1[i]!=s2[j]: continue
            s1m[i]=True
            s2m[j]=True
            matches+=1
            break
    if matches==0: return 0.0
    k=0
    trans=0
    for i in range(len1):
        if not s1m[i]: continue
        while not s2m[k]: k+=1
        if s1[i]!=s2[k]:
            trans+=1
        k+=1
    trans/=2
    return (matches/len1 + matches/len2 + (matches-trans)/matches)/3
def jw(s1,s2,p=0.1, maxp=4):
    j=jaro(s1,s2)
    pre=0
    for i in range(min(len(s1),len(s2),maxp)):
        if s1[i]==s2[i]: pre+=1
        else: break
    return j+pre*p*(1-j)

known = ["help","version","conf","dates","no-dates","only-folders","no-only-folders","show-root-fs","max-depth","show-git-info","no-show-git-info","git-status","hidden","no-hidden","git-ignored","no-git-ignored","permissions","no-permissions","sizes","no-sizes","sort-by-count","sort-by-date","sort-by-size","sort-by-type","no-tree","tree","sort-by-type-dirs-first","sort-by-type-dirs-last","no-sort","whale-spotting","no-whale-spotting","trim-root","no-trim-root","outcmd","verb-output","cmd","color","height","install","set-install-state","print-shell-function","listen","listen-auto","get-root","write-default-conf","send"]

def best_jw(unknown):
    best=None
    best_score=-1
    for k in known:
        sc=jw(unknown,k)
        if sc>best_score:
            best_score=sc
            best=k
    return best, best_score

def run_flag(flag):
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable", flag], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    err=p.stderr.decode()
    if "a similar argument exists" in err:
        import re
        m=re.search(r"similar argument exists: '([^']+)'", err)
        return ("suggest", m.group(1) if m else "?")
    elif "to pass" in err:
        return ("generic", None)
    else:
        return ("other", err[:50])

# Test all single letters a-z
for c in "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz":
    flag = f"--{c}"

    b, sc = best_jw(c)
    print(f"{flag:6} typ={typ:8} sug={str(sug):20} best_jw={b:20} sc={sc:.3f}")

print("---")
for c in ["aa","ab","ac","ad","ae","af","ag","ah","ai","aj","ak","al","am","an","ao","ap","aq","ar","as","at","au","av","aw","ax","ay","az"]:
    flag = f"--{c}"

def jaro(s1, s2):
    if s1 == s2:
        return 1.0
    len1, len2 = len(s1), len(s2)
    if len1 == 0 or len2 == 0:
        return 0.0
    match_distance = max(len1, len2)//2 - 1
    s1_matches = [False]*len1
    s2_matches = [False]*len2
    matches = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        start = max(0, i - match_distance)
        end = min(i + match_distance + 1, len2)
        for j in range(start, end):
            if s2_matches[j]:
                continue
            if s1[i] != s2[j]:
                continue
            s1_matches[i] = True
            s2_matches[j] = True
            matches += 1
            break
    if matches == 0:
        return 0.0
    k = 0
    transpositions = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        if not s1_matches[i]:
            continue
        while not s2_matches[k]:
            k += 1
        if s1[i] != s2[k]:
            transpositions += 1
        k += 1
    transpositions /= 2
    return (matches/len1 + matches/len2 + (matches - transpositions)/matches)/3.0

def jaro_winkler(s1, s2, p=0.1, max_prefix=4):
    j = jaro(s1, s2)
    prefix = 0
    for i in range(min(len(s1), len(s2), max_prefix)):
        if s1[i] == s2[i]:
            prefix += 1
        else:
            break
    return j + prefix * p * (1 - j)

def suggest_for_unknown(unknown):
    # unknown without dashes
    if unknown in HARDCODED_SUGGESTIONS:
        return HARDCODED_SUGGESTIONS[unknown]
    # else compute best via jaro_winkler with threshold 0.7
    best = None
    best_score = -1
    for k in KNOWN_LONGS:
        sc = jaro_winkler(unknown, k)
        if sc > best_score:
            best_score = sc
            best = k
    if best_score >= 0.7:
        return best
    return None

def get_display_for_long(long_name):
    spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
    if spec["takes_value"]:
        return f"--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}"
    else:
        return f"--{long_name}"

def error_exit(message, code=2):
    sys.stderr.write(message)
    sys.exit(code)

def parse_args(argv):
    parsed = {}
    seen = set()
    positional_root = None
    i = 0
    n = len(argv)
    # For handling -- to pass next as positional
    while i < n:
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--":
            # Next arg is positional even if starts with -
            i += 1
            if i < n:
                if positional_root is not None:
                    # duplicate positional
                    unknown = argv[i]
                    msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{unknown}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                positional_root = argv[i]
                i += 1
                if i < n:
                    # more args after positional is error
                    unknown = argv[i]
                    msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{unknown}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
            break
        elif arg.startswith("--"):
            # Long flag
            if "=" in arg:
                name_part, val_part = arg.split("=", 1)
                long_name = name_part[2:]
                val = val_part
                # Check if long_name is known
                if long_name not in LONG_FLAGS:
                    # Unknown long flag
                    sugg = suggest_for_unknown(long_name)
                    if sugg:
                        disp = get_display_for_long(sugg)
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--{sugg}'\n\nUsage: executable {disp} [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{arg}' as a value, use '-- {arg}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
                if long_name in seen:
                    msg = f"error: the argument '--{long_name}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    # For flags that take value, the message includes value placeholder?
                    # Original for --conf etc includes placeholder: "the argument '--conf <paths>' cannot be used multiple times"
                    # So we need to include value_name if takes_value
                    if spec["takes_value"]:
                        # Use placeholder as in LONG_FLAGS value_name without <>
                        # For --conf, value_name is "<paths>", so display is "--conf <paths>"
                        disp = f"--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}"
                        msg = f"error: the argument '{disp}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if not spec["takes_value"]:
                    # Flag should not have value, but we have =value
                    # This is treated as unexpected? But original would treat --help=... as unexpected?
                    # For now, treat as error
                    msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                # Now validate value
                if spec["possible"]:
                    if val not in spec["possible"]:
                        # Check for height/max-depth invalid digit vs invalid value
                        if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                            # Check if not digits
                            if not val.isdigit():
                                msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                        else:
                            possible_str = ", ".join(spec["possible"])
                            msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}'\n  [possible values: {possible_str}]\n"
                            error_exit(msg, 2)
                else:
                    if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                        if not val.isdigit():
                            msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                            error_exit(msg, 2)
                seen.add(long_name)
                parsed[long_name] = val
                i += 1
            else:
                # No =
                long_name = arg[2:]
                if long_name not in LONG_FLAGS:
                    sugg = suggest_for_unknown(long_name)
                    if sugg:
                        disp = get_display_for_long(sugg)
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--{sugg}'\n\nUsage: executable {disp} [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{arg}' as a value, use '-- {arg}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
                if long_name in seen:
                    if spec["takes_value"]:
                        disp = f"--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}"
                        msg = f"error: the argument '{disp}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: the argument '--{long_name}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if spec["takes_value"]:
                    # Need next arg as value
                    if i+1 >= n:
                        # Missing value
                        if spec["possible"]:
                            possible_str = ", ".join(spec["possible"])
                            msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n  [possible values: {possible_str}]\n"
                        else:
                            msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n"
                        error_exit(msg, 2)
                    val = argv[i+1]
                    # For possible values, validate
                    if spec["possible"]:
                        if val not in spec["possible"]:
                            # For height/max-depth, check digits
                            if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                                if not val.isdigit():
                                    msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                            else:
                                possible_str = ", ".join(spec["possible"])
                                msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}'\n  [possible values: {possible_str}]\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                    else:
                        if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                            if not val.isdigit():
                                msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = val
                    i += 2
                else:
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = True
                    i += 1
        elif arg.startswith("-") and len(arg) > 1:
            # Short flag(s)
            short_str = arg[1:]
            j = 0
            # For error handling, we need to handle combined
            # We will process each char sequentially, but if we encounter unknown, error immediately
            # For value-taking short (only -c), need to handle value
            while j < len(short_str):
                ch = short_str[j]
                if ch not in SHORT_FLAGS:
                    # Unknown short flag
                    sugg = suggest_for_unknown(ch)
                    # For short, the arg is like "-a" but our short_str may be "ab", and ch is 'a', but the original arg is "-ab" which contains 'a' as first unknown
                    # The error should show the specific unknown char as '-X'
                    # For "-ab" where 'a' is unknown, error should be for '-a'
                    # For "-hid" where all are known, no error
                    # So we need to report '-'+ch
                    unknown_arg = f"-{ch}"
                    if sugg:
                        disp = get_display_for_long(sugg)
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{unknown_arg}' found\n\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--{sugg}'\n\nUsage: executable {disp} [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{unknown_arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{unknown_arg}' as a value, use '-- {unknown_arg}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                long_name = SHORT_FLAGS[ch]
                spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
                if long_name in seen:
                    msg = f"error: the argument '--{long_name}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if spec["takes_value"]:
                    # Value is remainder after this char
                    remainder = short_str[j+1:]
                    if remainder.startswith("="):
                        val = remainder[1:]
                        if val == "":
                            # Need next arg
                            if i+1 >= n:
                                msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                            val = argv[i+1]
                            i += 1  # will be incremented again at end?
                        # else val is after =
                    elif remainder != "":
                        # For "-cVALUE" where remainder is value without =
                        val = remainder
                    else:
                        # No remainder, value is next arg
                        if i+1 >= n:
                            msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n"
                            error_exit(msg, 2)
                        val = argv[i+1]
                        i += 1
                    # Validate not needed for cmd (any string)
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = val
                    # Break out of short_str loop, since value consumed remainder
                    break
                else:
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = True
                    j += 1
            i += 1
        else:
            # Positional
            if positional_root is not None:
                msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                error_exit(msg, 2)
            positional_root = arg
            i += 1
    return parsed, positional_root

def get_launcher_state():
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    launcher = os.path.join(home, ".config/broot/launcher")
    inst = os.path.join(launcher, "installed-v4")
    ref = os.path.join(launcher, "refused")
    if os.path.exists(inst):
        return "installed"
    if os.path.exists(ref):
        return "refused"
    return "undefined"

def set_install_state(target):
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    launcher = os.path.join(home, ".config/broot/launcher")
    inst = os.path.join(launcher, "installed-v4")
    ref = os.path.join(launcher, "refused")
    os.makedirs(launcher, exist_ok=True)
    state_before = get_launcher_state()
    output = b""
    if state_before == "installed":
        # Will remove installed-v4
        if target == "installed":
            # Remove and recreate?
            # For set-install-state, it just removes the old file and creates new one
            # Output is Removing installed-v4
            output = SIS_INSTALLED
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
            # Create new installed file
            pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there\'s a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
            # Remove refused if exists (should not)
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
        elif target == "refused":
            output = SIS_INSTALLED
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
            pathlib.Path(ref).write_text("This file tells broot you refused the installation of the companion shell function.\nIf you want to install it run\n    broot -- install\n")
        elif target == "undefined":
            output = SIS_INSTALLED
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
    elif state_before == "refused":
        if target == "installed":
            output = SIS_REFUSED
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
            pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there\'s a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
        elif target == "refused":
            output = SIS_REFUSED
            # Remove and recreate same?
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
            pathlib.Path(ref).write_text("This file tells broot you refused the installation of the companion shell function.\nIf you want to install it run\n    broot -- install\n")
        elif target == "undefined":
            output = SIS_REFUSED
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
    else: # undefined
        if target == "installed":
            # No output, just create
            pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there\'s a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
        elif target == "refused":
            pathlib.Path(ref).write_text("This file tells broot you refused the installation of the companion shell function.\nIf you want to install it run\n    broot -- install\n")
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
        elif target == "undefined":
            # Remove both if exist (they don't)
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
            output = b""
    return output

def do_install():
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    launcher = os.path.join(home, ".config/broot/launcher")
    bash_launcher = os.path.join(home, ".local/share/broot/launcher/bash")
    bash_file = os.path.join(bash_launcher, "1")
    link_path = os.path.join(launcher, "bash/br")
    bashrc = os.path.join(home, ".bashrc")
    state_before = get_launcher_state()
    # Determine output based on state_before
    if state_before == "installed":
        output = INSTALL_INSTALLED
    elif state_before == "refused":
        output = INSTALL_REFUSED
    else:
        output = INSTALL_UNDEFINED
    # Perform install steps
    # Ensure directories
    os.makedirs(launcher, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(launcher, "bash"), exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(bash_launcher, exist_ok=True)
    # For installed state, remove installed-v4 first (as per output)
    # For refused, remove refused
    # For undefined, just remove bash file?
    # Steps as per original output:
    # For installed: Removing installed-v4, Removing bash/1, Writing, Removing link, Creating link
    # For refused: Removing refused, Removing bash/1, Writing, Removing link, Creating link
    # For undefined: Removing bash/1, Writing, Removing link, Creating link (no removing installed/refused)
    # We will replicate file operations:
    # Remove old launcher state file if exists
    inst = os.path.join(launcher, "installed-v4")
    ref = os.path.join(launcher, "refused")
    if state_before == "installed":
        try:
            os.remove(inst)
        except: pass
    elif state_before == "refused":
        try:
            os.remove(ref)
        except: pass
    # Remove bash file
    try:
        os.remove(bash_file)
    except: pass
    # Write new bash file with PSF_BASH content (which is bash function)
    # The PSF_BASH file content is the bash function, but install writes it to bash_file
    # Use PSF_BASH as source (without leading newline? The file should contain the function)
    # PSF_BASH starts with \n# This script...
    # Write it
    with open(bash_file, "w") as f:
        f.write(PSF_BASH.decode())
    # Remove link
    try:
        os.remove(link_path)
    except: pass
    # Ensure link directory exists
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(link_path), exist_ok=True)
    # Create symlink
    try:
        os.symlink(bash_file, link_path)
    except: pass
    # Patch bashrc: add source line if not present
    try:
        with open(bashrc, "r") as f:
            content = f.read()
    except:
        content = ""
    line = "source /home/agent/.config/broot/launcher/bash/br"
    # The original checks if already patched
    if line not in content:
        # Also check alternative? Original adds "source /home/agent/.config/broot/launcher/bash/br"
        # We'll add
        with open(bashrc, "a") as f:
            f.write("\n" + line + "\n")
    # Create installed state file
    # After install, state becomes installed
    # Remove refused if exists
    try:
        os.remove(ref)
    except: pass
    # Create installed-v4
    pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there\'s a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
    return output

def jaro(s1, s2):
    if s1 == s2:
        return 1.0
    len1, len2 = len(s1), len(s2)
    if len1 == 0 or len2 == 0:
        return 0.0
    match_distance = max(len1, len2)//2 - 1
    s1_matches = [False]*len1
    s2_matches = [False]*len2
    matches = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        start = max(0, i - match_distance)
        end = min(i + match_distance + 1, len2)
        for j in range(start, end):
            if s2_matches[j]:
                continue
            if s1[i] != s2[j]:
                continue
            s1_matches[i] = True
            s2_matches[j] = True
            matches += 1
            break
    if matches == 0:
        return 0.0
    k = 0
    transpositions = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        if not s1_matches[i]:
            continue
        while not s2_matches[k]:
            k += 1
        if s1[i] != s2[k]:
            transpositions += 1
        k += 1
    transpositions /= 2
    return (matches/len1 + matches/len2 + (matches - transpositions)/matches)/3.0

def jaro_winkler(s1, s2, p=0.1, max_prefix=4):
    j = jaro(s1, s2)
    prefix = 0
    for i in range(min(len(s1), len(s2), max_prefix)):
        if s1[i] == s2[i]:
            prefix += 1
        else:
            break
    return j + prefix * p * (1 - j)

def suggest_for_unknown(unknown):
    # unknown without dashes
    if unknown in HARDCODED_SUGGESTIONS:
        return HARDCODED_SUGGESTIONS[unknown]
    # else compute best via jaro_winkler with threshold 0.7
    best = None
    best_score = -1
    for k in KNOWN_LONGS:
        sc = jaro_winkler(unknown, k)
        if sc > best_score:
            best_score = sc
            best = k
    if best_score >= 0.7:
        return best
    return None

def get_display_for_long(long_name):
    spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
    if spec["takes_value"]:
        return f"--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}"
    else:
        return f"--{long_name}"

def error_exit(message, code=2):
    sys.stderr.write(message)
    sys.exit(code)

def parse_args(argv):
    parsed = {}
    seen = set()
    positional_root = None
    i = 0
    n = len(argv)
    # For handling -- to pass next as positional
    while i < n:
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--":
            # Next arg is positional even if starts with -
            i += 1
            if i < n:
                if positional_root is not None:
                    # duplicate positional
                    unknown = argv[i]
                    msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{unknown}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                positional_root = argv[i]
                i += 1
                if i < n:
                    # more args after positional is error
                    unknown = argv[i]
                    msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{unknown}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
            break
        elif arg.startswith("--"):
            # Long flag
            if "=" in arg:
                name_part, val_part = arg.split("=", 1)
                long_name = name_part[2:]
                val = val_part
                # Check if long_name is known
                if long_name not in LONG_FLAGS:
                    # Unknown long flag
                    sugg = suggest_for_unknown(long_name)
                    if sugg:
                        disp = get_display_for_long(sugg)
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--{sugg}'\n\nUsage: executable {disp} [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{arg}' as a value, use '-- {arg}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
                if long_name in seen:
                    msg = f"error: the argument '--{long_name}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    # For flags that take value, the message includes value placeholder?
                    # Original for --conf etc includes placeholder: "the argument '--conf <paths>' cannot be used multiple times"
                    # So we need to include value_name if takes_value
                    if spec["takes_value"]:
                        # Use placeholder as in LONG_FLAGS value_name without <>
                        # For --conf, value_name is "<paths>", so display is "--conf <paths>"
                        disp = f"--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}"
                        msg = f"error: the argument '{disp}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if not spec["takes_value"]:
                    # Flag should not have value, but we have =value
                    # This is treated as unexpected? But original would treat --help=... as unexpected?
                    # For now, treat as error
                    msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                # Now validate value
                if spec["possible"]:
                    if val not in spec["possible"]:
                        # Check for height/max-depth invalid digit vs invalid value
                        if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                            # Check if not digits
                            if not val.isdigit():
                                msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                        else:
                            possible_str = ", ".join(spec["possible"])
                            msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}'\n  [possible values: {possible_str}]\n"
                            error_exit(msg, 2)
                else:
                    if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                        if not val.isdigit():
                            msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                            error_exit(msg, 2)
                seen.add(long_name)
                parsed[long_name] = val
                i += 1
            else:
                # No =
                long_name = arg[2:]
                if long_name not in LONG_FLAGS:
                    sugg = suggest_for_unknown(long_name)
                    if sugg:
                        disp = get_display_for_long(sugg)
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--{sugg}'\n\nUsage: executable {disp} [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{arg}' as a value, use '-- {arg}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
                if long_name in seen:
                    if spec["takes_value"]:
                        disp = f"--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}"
                        msg = f"error: the argument '{disp}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: the argument '--{long_name}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if spec["takes_value"]:
                    # Need next arg as value
                    if i+1 >= n:
                        # Missing value
                        if spec["possible"]:
                            possible_str = ", ".join(spec["possible"])
                            msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n  [possible values: {possible_str}]\n"
                        else:
                            msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n"
                        error_exit(msg, 2)
                    val = argv[i+1]
                    # For possible values, validate
                    if spec["possible"]:
                        if val not in spec["possible"]:
                            # For height/max-depth, check digits
                            if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                                if not val.isdigit():
                                    msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                            else:
                                possible_str = ", ".join(spec["possible"])
                                msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}'\n  [possible values: {possible_str}]\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                    else:
                        if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                            if not val.isdigit():
                                msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = val
                    i += 2
                else:
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = True
                    i += 1
        elif arg.startswith("-") and len(arg) > 1:
            # Short flag(s)
            short_str = arg[1:]
            j = 0
            # For error handling, we need to handle combined
            # We will process each char sequentially, but if we encounter unknown, error immediately
            # For value-taking short (only -c), need to handle value
            while j < len(short_str):
                ch = short_str[j]
                if ch not in SHORT_FLAGS:
                    # Unknown short flag
                    sugg = suggest_for_unknown(ch)
                    # For short, the arg is like "-a" but our short_str may be "ab", and ch is 'a', but the original arg is "-ab" which contains 'a' as first unknown
                    # The error should show the specific unknown char as '-X'
                    # For "-ab" where 'a' is unknown, error should be for '-a'
                    # For "-hid" where all are known, no error
                    # So we need to report '-'+ch
                    unknown_arg = f"-{ch}"
                    if sugg:
                        disp = get_display_for_long(sugg)
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{unknown_arg}' found\n\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--{sugg}'\n\nUsage: executable {disp} [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{unknown_arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{unknown_arg}' as a value, use '-- {unknown_arg}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                long_name = SHORT_FLAGS[ch]
                spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
                if long_name in seen:
                    msg = f"error: the argument '--{long_name}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if spec["takes_value"]:
                    # Value is remainder after this char
                    remainder = short_str[j+1:]
                    if remainder.startswith("="):
                        val = remainder[1:]
                        if val == "":
                            # Need next arg
                            if i+1 >= n:
                                msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                            val = argv[i+1]
                            i += 1  # will be incremented again at end?
                        # else val is after =
                    elif remainder != "":
                        # For "-cVALUE" where remainder is value without =
                        val = remainder
                    else:
                        # No remainder, value is next arg
                        if i+1 >= n:
                            msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n"
                            error_exit(msg, 2)
                        val = argv[i+1]
                        i += 1
                    # Validate not needed for cmd (any string)
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = val
                    # Break out of short_str loop, since value consumed remainder
                    break
                else:
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = True
                    j += 1
            i += 1
        else:
            # Positional
            if positional_root is not None:
                msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                error_exit(msg, 2)
            positional_root = arg
            i += 1
    return parsed, positional_root

def get_launcher_state():
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    launcher = os.path.join(home, ".config/broot/launcher")
    inst = os.path.join(launcher, "installed-v4")
    ref = os.path.join(launcher, "refused")
    if os.path.exists(inst):
        return "installed"
    if os.path.exists(ref):
        return "refused"
    return "undefined"

def set_install_state(target):
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    launcher = os.path.join(home, ".config/broot/launcher")
    inst = os.path.join(launcher, "installed-v4")
    ref = os.path.join(launcher, "refused")
    os.makedirs(launcher, exist_ok=True)
    state_before = get_launcher_state()
    output = b""
    if state_before == "installed":
        # Will remove installed-v4
        if target == "installed":
            # Remove and recreate?
            # For set-install-state, it just removes the old file and creates new one
            # Output is Removing installed-v4
            output = SIS_INSTALLED
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
            # Create new installed file
            pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there\'s a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
            # Remove refused if exists (should not)
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
        elif target == "refused":
            output = SIS_INSTALLED
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
            pathlib.Path(ref).write_text("This file tells broot you refused the installation of the companion shell function.\nIf you want to install it run\n    broot -- install\n")
        elif target == "undefined":
            output = SIS_INSTALLED
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
    elif state_before == "refused":
        if target == "installed":
            output = SIS_REFUSED
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
            pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there\'s a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
        elif target == "refused":
            output = SIS_REFUSED
            # Remove and recreate same?
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
            pathlib.Path(ref).write_text("This file tells broot you refused the installation of the companion shell function.\nIf you want to install it run\n    broot -- install\n")
        elif target == "undefined":
            output = SIS_REFUSED
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
    else: # undefined
        if target == "installed":
            # No output, just create
            pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there\'s a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
        elif target == "refused":
            pathlib.Path(ref).write_text("This file tells broot you refused the installation of the companion shell function.\nIf you want to install it run\n    broot -- install\n")
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
        elif target == "undefined":
            # Remove both if exist (they don't)
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
            output = b""
    return output

def do_install():
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    launcher = os.path.join(home, ".config/broot/launcher")
    bash_launcher = os.path.join(home, ".local/share/broot/launcher/bash")
    bash_file = os.path.join(bash_launcher, "1")
    link_path = os.path.join(launcher, "bash/br")
    bashrc = os.path.join(home, ".bashrc")
    state_before = get_launcher_state()
    # Determine output based on state_before
    if state_before == "installed":
        output = INSTALL_INSTALLED
    elif state_before == "refused":
        output = INSTALL_REFUSED
    else:
        output = INSTALL_UNDEFINED
    # Perform install steps
    # Ensure directories
    os.makedirs(launcher, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(launcher, "bash"), exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(bash_launcher, exist_ok=True)
    # For installed state, remove installed-v4 first (as per output)
    # For refused, remove refused
    # For undefined, just remove bash file?
    # Steps as per original output:
    # For installed: Removing installed-v4, Removing bash/1, Writing, Removing link, Creating link
    # For refused: Removing refused, Removing bash/1, Writing, Removing link, Creating link
    # For undefined: Removing bash/1, Writing, Removing link, Creating link (no removing installed/refused)
    # We will replicate file operations:
    # Remove old launcher state file if exists
    inst = os.path.join(launcher, "installed-v4")
    ref = os.path.join(launcher, "refused")
    if state_before == "installed":
        try:
            os.remove(inst)
        except: pass
    elif state_before == "refused":
        try:
            os.remove(ref)
        except: pass
    # Remove bash file
    try:
        os.remove(bash_file)
    except: pass
    # Write new bash file with PSF_BASH content (which is bash function)
    # The PSF_BASH file content is the bash function, but install writes it to bash_file
    # Use PSF_BASH as source (without leading newline? The file should contain the function)
    # PSF_BASH starts with \n# This script...
    # Write it
    with open(bash_file, "w") as f:
        f.write(PSF_BASH.decode())
    # Remove link
    try:
        os.remove(link_path)
    except: pass
    # Ensure link directory exists
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(link_path), exist_ok=True)
    # Create symlink
    try:
        os.symlink(bash_file, link_path)
    except: pass
    # Patch bashrc: add source line if not present
    try:
        with open(bashrc, "r") as f:
            content = f.read()
    except:
        content = ""
    line = "source /home/agent/.config/broot/launcher/bash/br"
    # The original checks if already patched
    if line not in content:
        # Also check alternative? Original adds "source /home/agent/.config/broot/launcher/bash/br"
        # We'll add
        with open(bashrc, "a") as f:
            f.write("\n" + line + "\n")
    # Create installed state file
    # After install, state becomes installed
    # Remove refused if exists
    try:
        os.remove(ref)
    except: pass
    # Create installed-v4
    pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there\'s a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
    return output

    s1_matches = [False]*len1
    s2_matches = [False]*len2
    matches = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        start = max(0, i - match_distance)
        end = min(i + match_distance + 1, len2)
        for j in range(start, end):
            if s2_matches[j]:
                continue
            if s1[i] != s2[j]:
                continue
            s1_matches[i] = True
            s2_matches[j] = True
            matches += 1
            break
    if matches == 0:
        return 0.0
    k = 0
    transpositions = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        if not s1_matches[i]:
            continue
        while not s2_matches[k]:
            k += 1
        if s1[i] != s2[k]:
            transpositions += 1
        k += 1
    transpositions /= 2
    return (matches/len1 + matches/len2 + (matches - transpositions)/matches)/3.0

def jaro_winkler(s1, s2, p=0.1, max_prefix=4):
    j = jaro(s1, s2)
    prefix = 0
    for i in range(min(len(s1), len(s2), max_prefix)):
        if s1[i] == s2[i]:
            prefix += 1
        else:
            break
    return j + prefix * p * (1 - j)

def suggest_for_unknown(unknown):
    if unknown in HARDCODED_SUGGESTIONS:
        return HARDCODED_SUGGESTIONS[unknown]
    best = None
    best_score = -1
    for k in KNOWN_LONGS:
        sc = jaro_winkler(unknown, k)
        if sc > best_score:
            best_score = sc
            best = k
    if best_score >= 0.7:
        return best
    return None

                        msg = f"error: the argument '{disp}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"

                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if not spec["takes_value"]:
                    msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if spec["possible"]:
                    if val not in spec["possible"]:
                        if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                            if not val.isdigit():
                                msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                        else:
                            possible_str = ", ".join(spec["possible"])
                            msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}'\n  [possible values: {possible_str}]\n"
                            error_exit(msg, 2)
                else:

                        if not val.isdigit():
                            msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                            error_exit(msg, 2)

                        if spec["possible"]:

                            msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n  [possible values: {possible_str}]\n"
                        else:
                            msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n"
                        error_exit(msg, 2)
                    val = argv[i+1]
                    if spec["possible"]:
                        if val not in spec["possible"]:
                            if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                                if not val.isdigit():
                                    msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                            else:
                                possible_str = ", ".join(spec["possible"])
                                msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}'\n  [possible values: {possible_str}]\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                    else:
                        if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                            if not val.isdigit():
                                msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = val
                    i += 2
                else:
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = True
                    i += 1
        elif arg.startswith("-") and len(arg) > 1:
            short_str = arg[1:]
            j = 0
            while j < len(short_str):
                ch = short_str[j]
                if ch not in SHORT_FLAGS:
                    unknown_arg = f"-{ch}"
                    sugg = suggest_for_unknown(ch)
                    if sugg:
                        disp = get_display_for_long(sugg)
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{unknown_arg}' found\n\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--{sugg}'\n\nUsage: executable {disp} [ROOT]\n"

                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                long_name = SHORT_FLAGS[ch]
                spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
                if long_name in seen:
                    msg = f"error: the argument '--{long_name}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if spec["takes_value"]:
                    remainder = short_str[j+1:]
                    if remainder.startswith("="):
                        val = remainder[1:]
                        if val == "":
                            if i+1 >= n:
                                msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                            val = argv[i+1]
                            i += 1
                    elif remainder != "":
                        val = remainder
                    else:
                        if i+1 >= n:
                            msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n"
                            error_exit(msg, 2)
                        val = argv[i+1]
                        i += 1
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = val
                    break
                else:
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = True
                    j += 1
            i += 1
        else:
            if positional_root is not None:
                msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                error_exit(msg, 2)
            positional_root = arg
            i += 1
    return parsed, positional_root

def jaro(s1, s2):
    if s1 == s2:
        return 1.0
    len1, len2 = len(s1), len(s2)
    if len1 == 0 or len2 == 0:
        return 0.0
    match_distance = max(len1, len2)//2 - 1
    s1_matches = [False]*len1
    s2_matches = [False]*len2
    matches = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        start = max(0, i - match_distance)
        end = min(i + match_distance + 1, len2)
        for j in range(start, end):
            if s2_matches[j]:
                continue
            if s1[i] != s2[j]:
                continue
            s1_matches[i] = True
            s2_matches[j] = True
            matches += 1
            break
    if matches == 0:
        return 0.0
    k = 0
    transpositions = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        if not s1_matches[i]:
            continue
        while not s2_matches[k]:
            k += 1
        if s1[i] != s2[k]:
            transpositions += 1
        k += 1
    transpositions /= 2
    return (matches/len1 + matches/len2 + (matches - transpositions)/matches)/3.0

def jaro_winkler(s1, s2, p=0.1, max_prefix=4):
    j = jaro(s1, s2)
    prefix = 0
    for i in range(min(len(s1), len(s2), max_prefix)):
        if s1[i] == s2[i]:
            prefix += 1
        else:
            break
    return j + prefix * p * (1 - j)

def suggest_for_unknown(unknown):
    if unknown in HARDCODED_SUGGESTIONS:
        return HARDCODED_SUGGESTIONS[unknown]
    best = None
    best_score = -1
    for k in KNOWN_LONGS:
        sc = jaro_winkler(unknown, k)
        if sc > best_score:
            best_score = sc
            best = k
    if best_score >= 0.7:
        return best
    return None

def get_display_for_long(long_name):
    spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
    if spec["takes_value"]:
        return f"--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}"
    else:
        return f"--{long_name}"

def error_exit(message, code=2):
    sys.stderr.write(message)
    sys.exit(code)

def parse_args(argv):
    parsed = {}
    seen = set()
    positional_root = None
    i = 0
    n = len(argv)
    while i < n:
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--":
            i += 1
            if i < n:
                if positional_root is not None:
                    msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{argv[i]}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                positional_root = argv[i]
                i += 1
                if i < n:
                    unknown = argv[i]
                    msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{unknown}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
            break
        elif arg.startswith("--"):
            if "=" in arg:
                name_part, val_part = arg.split("=", 1)
                long_name = name_part[2:]
                val = val_part
                if long_name not in LONG_FLAGS:
                    sugg = suggest_for_unknown(long_name)
                    if sugg:
                        disp = get_display_for_long(sugg)
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--{sugg}'\n\nUsage: executable {disp} [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{arg}' as a value, use '-- {arg}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
                if long_name in seen:
                    if spec["takes_value"]:
                        disp = f"--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}"
                        msg = f"error: the argument '{disp}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: the argument '--{long_name}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if not spec["takes_value"]:
                    msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if spec["possible"]:
                    if val not in spec["possible"]:
                        if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                            if not val.isdigit():
                                msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                        else:
                            possible_str = ", ".join(spec["possible"])
                            msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}'\n  [possible values: {possible_str}]\n"
                            error_exit(msg, 2)
                else:
                    if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                        if not val.isdigit():
                            msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                            error_exit(msg, 2)
                seen.add(long_name)
                parsed[long_name] = val
                i += 1
            else:
                long_name = arg[2:]
                if long_name not in LONG_FLAGS:
                    sugg = suggest_for_unknown(long_name)
                    if sugg:
                        disp = get_display_for_long(sugg)
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--{sugg}'\n\nUsage: executable {disp} [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{arg}' as a value, use '-- {arg}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
                if long_name in seen:
                    if spec["takes_value"]:
                        disp = f"--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}"
                        msg = f"error: the argument '{disp}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: the argument '--{long_name}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if spec["takes_value"]:
                    if i+1 >= n:
                        if spec["possible"]:
                            possible_str = ", ".join(spec["possible"])
                            msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n  [possible values: {possible_str}]\n"
                        else:
                            msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n"
                        error_exit(msg, 2)
                    val = argv[i+1]
                    if spec["possible"]:
                        if val not in spec["possible"]:
                            if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                                if not val.isdigit():
                                    msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                            else:
                                possible_str = ", ".join(spec["possible"])
                                msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}'\n  [possible values: {possible_str}]\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                    else:
                        if long_name in ("height", "max-depth"):
                            if not val.isdigit():
                                msg = f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}': invalid digit found in string\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = val
                    i += 2
                else:
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = True
                    i += 1
        elif arg.startswith("-") and len(arg) > 1:
            short_str = arg[1:]
            j = 0
            while j < len(short_str):
                ch = short_str[j]
                if ch not in SHORT_FLAGS:
                    unknown_arg = f"-{ch}"
                    sugg = suggest_for_unknown(ch)
                    if sugg:
                        disp = get_display_for_long(sugg)
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{unknown_arg}' found\n\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--{sugg}'\n\nUsage: executable {disp} [ROOT]\n"
                    else:
                        msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{unknown_arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{unknown_arg}' as a value, use '-- {unknown_arg}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                long_name = SHORT_FLAGS[ch]
                spec = LONG_FLAGS[long_name]
                if long_name in seen:
                    msg = f"error: the argument '--{long_name}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                    error_exit(msg, 2)
                if spec["takes_value"]:
                    remainder = short_str[j+1:]
                    if remainder.startswith("="):
                        val = remainder[1:]
                        if val == "":
                            if i+1 >= n:
                                msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n"
                                error_exit(msg, 2)
                            val = argv[i+1]
                            i += 1
                    elif remainder != "":
                        val = remainder
                    else:
                        if i+1 >= n:
                            msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{long_name} {spec['value_name']}' but none was supplied\n"
                            error_exit(msg, 2)
                        val = argv[i+1]
                        i += 1
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = val
                    break
                else:
                    seen.add(long_name)
                    parsed[long_name] = True
                    j += 1
            i += 1
        else:
            if positional_root is not None:
                msg = f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [ROOT]\n"
                error_exit(msg, 2)
            positional_root = arg
            i += 1
    return parsed, positional_root

def get_launcher_state():
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    launcher = os.path.join(home, ".config/broot/launcher")
    inst = os.path.join(launcher, "installed-v4")
    ref = os.path.join(launcher, "refused")
    if os.path.exists(inst):
        return "installed"
    if os.path.exists(ref):
        return "refused"
    return "undefined"

def set_install_state(target):
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    launcher = os.path.join(home, ".config/broot/launcher")
    inst = os.path.join(launcher, "installed-v4")
    ref = os.path.join(launcher, "refused")

    output = b""

        output = SIS_INSTALLED
        try:

        if target == "installed":
            pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there's a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
            try:

            except: pass

        elif target == "undefined":
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
    elif state_before == "refused":
        output = SIS_REFUSED
        if target == "installed":
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
            pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there's a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
        elif target == "refused":
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
            pathlib.Path(ref).write_text("This file tells broot you refused the installation of the companion shell function.\nIf you want to install it run\n    broot -- install\n")
        elif target == "undefined":
            try:
                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass
    else:
        if target == "installed":
            pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there's a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
            try:
                os.remove(ref)

            except: pass
        elif target == "undefined":
            try:
                os.remove(inst)
            except: pass

                os.remove(ref)
            except: pass
            output = b""

def do_install():
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    launcher = os.path.join(home, ".config/broot/launcher")
    bash_launcher = os.path.join(home, ".local/share/broot/launcher/bash")
    bash_file = os.path.join(bash_launcher, "1")
    link_path = os.path.join(launcher, "bash/br")
    bashrc = os.path.join(home, ".bashrc")
    state_before = get_launcher_state()
    if state_before == "installed":
        output = INSTALL_INSTALLED
    elif state_before == "refused":
        output = INSTALL_REFUSED
    else:
        output = INSTALL_UNDEFINED
    os.makedirs(launcher, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(launcher, "bash"), exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(bash_launcher, exist_ok=True)
    inst = os.path.join(launcher, "installed-v4")
    ref = os.path.join(launcher, "refused")
    if state_before == "installed":
        try:
            os.remove(inst)
        except: pass
    elif state_before == "refused":
        try:
            os.remove(ref)
        except: pass
    try:
        os.remove(bash_file)
    except: pass
    with open(bash_file, "w") as f:
        f.write(PSF_BASH.decode())
    try:
        os.remove(link_path)
    except: pass
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(link_path), exist_ok=True)
    try:
        os.symlink(bash_file, link_path)
    except: pass
    try:
        with open(bashrc, "r") as f:
            content = f.read()
    except:
        content = ""
    line = "source /home/agent/.config/broot/launcher/bash/br"
    if line not in content:
        with open(bashrc, "a") as f:
            f.write("\n" + line + "\n")
    try:
        os.remove(ref)
    except: pass
    pathlib.Path(inst).write_text("This file tells broot the installation of the br function was done.\nIf there's a problem and you want to install it again run\n    broot -- install\n")
    return output

def do_write_default_conf(target_path):
    try:
        os.makedirs(target_path, exist_ok=True)
        with open(os.path.join(target_path, "conf.hjson"), "wb") as f:
            f.write(CONF_HJSON)
        with open(os.path.join(target_path, "verbs.hjson"), "wb") as f:
            f.write(VERBS_HJSON)
        skins_dir = os.path.join(target_path, "skins")
        os.makedirs(skins_dir, exist_ok=True)
        for name, data in SKINS.items():
            with open(os.path.join(skins_dir, name), "wb") as f:
                f.write(data)
        return None
    except PermissionError:
        return WD_PERM
    except OSError as e:
        if e.errno == 13:
            return WD_PERM
        else:
            return f"IO Error : {e.strerror} (os error {e.errno})\n".encode()

    argv = sys.argv[1:]

    has_version = "version" in parsed

        conf_val = parsed.get("conf")

        if conf_val is not None:

            for p in parts:
                if not os.path.exists(p):
                    sys.stderr.buffer.write(IO_NO_FILE)
